meta.note: Curated grounding facts for Move2AD. source_type 'official' = government/regulator page; 'secondary' = reputable press/legal/industry source citing official data. Facts with needs_verification=true must be re-checked via web_search (allowed_domains) before being shown as definitive.

facts.claim: Abu Dhabi Golden Visa for skilled professionals: 10 years; must be employed in the UAE in a MOHRE Level 1 or 2 role; bachelor's degree or equivalent; minimum monthly salary AED 30,000; practising licence where required.

Abu Dhabi Golden Visa for entrepreneurs (10 years): owner/partner with a pioneering project approved by an approved incubator or the Ministry of Economy; OR owner of a pioneering project with annual revenue of at least AED 1,000,000; OR founder of previous project(s) sold for at least AED 7,000,000.
Abu Dhabi Golden Visa categories offer a 10-year residence permit that includes sponsorship of spouse and children irrespective of their age.
Golden Visa for talents in digital technology requires a recommendation from the Emirates Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions or a local competent authority.

Abu Dhabi Green Visa for skilled employees: 5 years, self-sponsored; work permit with a valid UAE employment contract; MOHRE Level 1, 2 or 3; bachelor's degree; minimum monthly salary AED 15,000. ADRO states nomination for this category is currently unavailable through Abu Dhabi Residents Office.

UAE Green Visa for freelancers (5 years, no sponsor): MOHRE freelance or self-employment permit, bachelor's degree or specialised diploma, and freelance income of at least AED 360,000 a year over the previous two years.

UAE job-seeker visit visa: 60, 90 or 120 days, one trip, no local sponsor needed, extendable up to 180 days in total. Eligible: MOHRE skill level 1, 2 or 3, or a graduate of a top-500 world university within the last two years; bachelor's degree or equivalent and a financial guarantee. Apply via ICP.
Job-seeker visa fees reported as AED 200 (60 days), AED 300 (90 days), AED 400 (120 days) plus 5% VAT and a refundable AED 1,000 security deposit.

Under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, the employer must bear all recruitment and employment costs (visa, residence permit, medical, etc.) and may not charge or recover them from the worker directly or indirectly. Any request for a 'visa fee' or deposit from a candidate is a major red flag.

MOHRE warns of fake job offers targeting people inside and outside the UAE: unsolicited WhatsApp offers, high salary with no interview, pressure to pay quickly, fees for visa/training/insurance/deposits, generic Gmail/Yahoo addresses, no UAE recruitment licence, visa documents sent as images on blank letterhead, payment links outside official .gov.ae domains.
A genuine UAE job offer issued through MOHRE carries a transaction/offer number that the candidate can look up on MOHRE's official Offer Inquiry service before signing anything or paying anyone.

Report a scam or fraud to Abu Dhabi Police: police stations are the competent authority for criminal reports. Aman (toll-free 800 2626) is the police's confidential 24/7 channel for tip-offs about crime. Keep all messages and payment receipts as evidence.
Abu Dhabi's population reached 4,135,985 in 2024, up 7.5% year on year and 51% over the past decade (2.7m in 2014).
Employment in Abu Dhabi grew 9.1% in 2024 to 2.76 million people. Blue-collar jobs grew 11.4% and white-collar jobs 6.4%, driven by large infrastructure and construction projects.
Strongest hiring areas in Abu Dhabi for 2026: technology/AI, financial services, healthcare, energy, logistics, infrastructure/construction, real estate and professional services.

UAE skills shortages in 2026 span technology, healthcare, construction, logistics and hospitality; skilled trades (electricians, welders, MEP technicians) remain in short supply; job postings requiring AI skills are rising fast.

Abu Dhabi's 'Thrive in Abu Dhabi' programme encourages global talent and investors to build their futures in the emirate, offering long-term visas and pathways in priority sectors such as healthcare, science, education, engineering and sport.
In the 2026 Arab Youth Survey, 57% of young Arabs chose the UAE as the country they would most like to live in — the highest since tracking began in 2012.
Abu Dhabi is home to more than 2.2 million expatriates of over 200 nationalities.
Abu Dhabi's Department of Community Development launched the Jiran Volunteer Programme at LIVEX 2026 to help new residents settle in, get to know their neighbours and find local services.

Abu Dhabi Residents Office (ADRO) helps new residents settle in: guidance on long-term residency and Golden Visa, welcome guides on housing, banking, education and healthcare, and community programmes.

TAMM is Abu Dhabi's unified government services platform: TAMM 4.0 offers over 1,100 public and private services and an AI assistant that can complete many services for you. Use it for transactions once you are a resident.

On 3 June 2026 the Government of Abu Dhabi cut the annual rent increase cap from 5% to 0% for residential, commercial and industrial properties, temporarily and until further notice. All renewals and new agreements reference the rent in the property's last registered Tawtheeq contract.

Tawtheeq is Abu Dhabi's official tenancy contract registration, done online through DARI or TAMM (AED 50 to register a new lease). A contract signed outside the online service is not a Tawtheeq contract. A registered Tawtheeq is commonly asked for when connecting water and electricity and for tenancy-linked services.

Every onshore Abu Dhabi property advert must carry a Madhmoun permit/QR code. Verify the permit and ownership via ADREC's Verify Document service and look up the broker in the ADREC directory. For Al Reem and Al Maryah islands use ADGM's registry. Never pay a deposit before viewing.

Typical annual rent for a 1-bedroom apartment (entry to premium): Khalifa City/MBZ City AED 40k–60k; Al Muroor/Airport Road AED 38k–58k; Al Khalidiyah/Corniche AED 50k–140k; Al Reem Island AED 55k–130k; Yas Island AED 65k–115k; Al Raha Beach AED 70k–125k; Saadiyat Island AED 85k–210k.

Upfront move-in costs beyond rent: security deposit (commonly 5% of annual rent), agency commission (2%), ADDC water/electricity deposit (about AED 1,000–2,500), municipality fee charged via ADDC bills as a percentage of annual rent, and district cooling (chiller) deposits of AED 500–2,000 where applicable.

Health insurance is mandatory in Abu Dhabi and provided by employers. The Daman Basic plan applies to expatriates earning up to AED 5,000/month (AED 4,000 with accommodation). Thiqa is for UAE nationals only.

Private school fees in Abu Dhabi for 2026 range roughly AED 27k–65k (KG), AED 35k–85k (primary), AED 45k–100k (secondary), AED 60k–110k (sixth form/IB). Popular British/American/IB schools have waitlists of 6–18 months; apply September–December for the next September intake.

To open a UAE bank account, banks usually ask for your Emirates ID, residence visa, passport and a salary certificate or employment letter. Many banks let you apply online or in their app, and approval takes from a few hours to a few days.

Hub71 Access Programme (pre-seed to Series A): AED 250,000 in-kind support plus AED 250,000 cash for equity via SAFE, and up to AED 250,000 more for top performers after a year; includes office, housing and health insurance support, licensing and visa assistance. At least one founder must relocate long-term to Abu Dhabi. Cohort 21 deadline: February 2027.
At LIVEX 2026 (29 September – 1 October), ADREC and Hub71 signed a two-year MoU that connects real estate sector challenges with startups through pilots, solution validation and mentorship.
